verdict: AutoZone's fourth-quarter sales rose 6% to $6.6B with same-store sales up 1.5%, and net income rose 11% to $932M (EPS $56.05) as relentless buybacks shrank the share count.

kpis.label: Stores
kpis.note: 175 opened in the quarter, incl. 68 in Mexico

segments.name: Auto parts stores
segments.note: AutoZone reports a single segment: 6,863 stores in the U.S., 1,001 in Mexico and 167 in Brazil, selling parts and accessories to do-it-yourself customers and professional garages, plus the ALLDATA repair-software business.

opex.name: Operating, selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Store payroll, rent and distribution — about a third of sales.

otherDetail: Interest expense, net of $149M on AutoZone's borrowings (the company runs with significant debt by design, funding buybacks).

takeaways.title: Sales rose to $6.6B
takeaways.text: Same-store sales grew 1.5% and 175 new stores (374 for the year) added the rest; full-year sales reached $20.3B.

takeaways.title: EPS jumped 15% to $56.05
takeaways.text: Profit rose 11%, but EPS rose faster: buybacks cut the diluted share count from 17.2M to 16.6M in a year — AutoZone has the highest share price of any U.S. auto-parts retailer.

takeaways.title: Gross margin of 53.3%
takeaways.text: More than half of every sales dollar survives the cost of the parts themselves — pricing power in a needs-based category.

footerNote: AutoZone combined its operations into a single reportable segment in fiscal 2025 and does not disclose a revenue split by country, so the full top line is shown as one source. The quarter is 16 weeks (AutoZone's fourth quarter is longer than the others).
